 PUB urges Singaporeans to make their own luck in flood readiness campaign via TBWA\Singapore 
 November 18 2026, 9:09 am | BY Adam Shaw | No Comments 
 In Singapore, “luckily” often punctuates stories of everyday close calls: luckily we left early, luckily we checked, luckily we took another route. We credit chance, even when a conscious decision helped things go our way.
 Flood readiness is one such aspect where people living in Singapore often rely on luck to get by, as they’d imagine it to be a rare occurrence with the proper infrastructure in place. However, sudden and unpredictable rainfall can temporarily overwhelm drains, causing flash floods, and with climate change, the risk will grow. While national water agency PUB’s ongoing flood management efforts have significantly reduced flood risks in Singapore, it’s impossible to eliminate floods entirely.
 Ahead of the northeast monsoon season, PUB and TBWA\Singapore has launched the Flood Resilience Campaign, “Luckily You Didn’t Rely on Luck”, which encourages people across Singapore to recognise the preparation behind what appears to be a lucky escape and make flood readiness a deliberate choice.
 Leading the campaign is a playful film starring a man with an enviable knack for being in the right place at the right time. Life seems to fall effortlessly into place for Singapore’s luckiest man. But when the weather turns, even he has something more reliable than luck to count on.
 Extending this idea across multiple touchpoints, the campaign brings flood readiness into everyday situations for commuters, motorists, business owners and the wider public. From checking the @pubfloodalerts Telegram channel or the myENV app for alerts before a journey to planning alternative routes and putting flood protection measures in place at business premises, each scenario shows how preparation trumps relying on luck.
 “Everyone has a part to play in building a more flood-resilient Singapore. Checking the weather before heading out, subscribing to flood alerts and knowing what to do during a flash flood can help keep everyone safe. Through this campaign, we hope to encourage Singaporeans to make these actions a habit.” said Ann Chan, Director of the 3P Network Department at PUB, Singapore’s National Water Agency.
 “At TBWA, we believe culture can unlock behavioural change. For this campaign, that part of culture was luck. ‘Luckily’ comes so naturally to us in Singapore. It’s how we describe a close shave or a day that went our way. We wanted to turn that familiar expression into a moment of recognition: if you checked an alert and avoided a flooded road, you made your own luck. Through humour and a charming visual world, we’re making flood preparedness feel simple, relevant and achievable,” said Loo Yong Ping, Executive Creative Director, TBWA\Singapore.
 “Luckily You Didn’t Rely on Luck” runs until 21 January 2027 across FTA, radio, social OOH and social media.
 To get flood-ready, visit https://go.gov.sg/befloodready and follow @pubfloodalerts on Telegram.
